data.narrative:
Path Robotics, a Series D robotics and manufacturing company founded by Andy and Alex Lonsberry, has raised $271M to date. Valuation analysis relies on two applicable triangulation methods against a peer set of five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: Divergent ($2.3B, Series E), Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Hadrian ($1.6B, Series C), Agile Robots ($1.0B, Series C), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B, Series C).

The stage-progression method applies a 1.5x step-up multiplier typical of Series D advancement, yielding $406M from the $271M raised proxy. The peer-median approach anchors to the $1.6B median valuation across the five comparables, with a stated range of $1.0B to $2.3B. These methods imply substantially different outcomes, reflecting the heterogeneity in peer-stage positioning and maturity.

Triangulation across both methods supports a valuation range of $346M (low bound) to $1.8B (high bound), with a median of $1.0B. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty: the stage-progression floor assumes minimal premium to capital deployed, while the peer-median ceiling reflects valuation multiples observed at more mature Series E and Series D stages. Path's positioning relative to Exotec (a direct Series D peer at $2.0B) and Hadrian (Series C at $1.6B) suggests the median range of $1.0B–$1.6B may be most defensible pending additional operational and revenue visibility.
